items.t: 42 houses sold in Guildford at a median of $1,145,000 (middle half $1,040,000 to $1,303,750). A typical house in Guildford spent 24 days on the market and closed at 95.0% of the asking price.
In Guildford, townhomes sold at a median of $640,000 across 78 sales, and the middle half closed between $508,250 and $766,000. The median townhome sat 38 days and sold for 97.2% of list.
Guildford: 92 condos sold at a median of $495,500, with the middle half between $406,500 and $535,250. The median condo took 26 days to sell and closed at 96.9% of list.

blocks.text: Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How Guildford compares with the rest of North Surrey

items.t: Houses in Guildford have the third highest median of 7 North Surrey sub-areas, $1,145,000. Bridgeview is lowest at $1,040,000 and Fraser Heights highest at $1,559,000. Royal Heights ($1,125,000) sits just below and Whalley ($1,305,000) sits just above.

Of 5 North Surrey sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Guildford ranks second lowest at $640,000; the range is $620,000 (Whalley) to $925,000 (Fraser Heights). Whalley ($620,000) sits just below and Cedar Hills ($817,500) sits just above.
Condos in Guildford have the highest median of the 4 North Surrey sub-areas, $495,500, ahead of Bolivar Heights at $460,000; the lowest is Cedar Hills at $325,900.

blocks.text: By build year, condos are the newest homes selling in Guildford (median 1997) and houses the oldest (median 1983), a gap of 14 years.
